facts.fact: Article 11 of loi n° 05-20 on cybersecurity (dahir n° 1-20-69 of 25 July 2020, Bulletin officiel n° 6906 of 6 August 2020) requires sensitive data to be hosted exclusively on national territory, with fines of 200,000 to 400,000 DH under article 49 for heads of vital entities or infrastructures hosting it abroad; article 53 makes the law operative only on publication of its implementing texts.
facts.system: Loi n° 05-20 relative à la cybersécurité, article 11

note: Rule published 2020-08-06; document says entry into force awaits implementing texts (art. 53) and does not say whether they were issued; no enforcer body named for the rule.

facts.fact: Hespress English, citing a Global Finance report, states that a 2021 law mandates sensitive data be stored locally in Morocco; the date is the article's published date, and the article gives no law name.
facts.system: 2021 law mandating local storage of sensitive data (unnamed)

note: Article only says the law has spurred data repatriation, with no organisation named or counted, so no fact on use.

facts.fact: A tribune by Oviasoft's founder says Morocco's draft 2027 finance bill provides for storing Moroccans' data in a sovereign national cloud.
Global Finance Magazine says a 2021 law ordered all sensitive data to be hosted within Morocco's borders, which led to data repatriation.
facts.system: 2021 law on hosting of sensitive data
